<a id="body"></a>

## Body

- A negative probe is not absence. On Darwin, connect() to a LIVE unix listener with a full backlog returns ECONNREFUSED, and tmux then prints "no server running on <path>". Prove "gone" with positive evidence: the server's own pid exiting (pij_core::program::process_exists, kill(pid,0)), or which socket files are bound (/proc/net/unix on Linux, or one bounded /usr/sbin/lsof -nP -a -U -u <uid> -F n on macOS; no unsafe in the workspace, and proc_pidinfo 0.1.4 has no socket fd info). Fail closed when the evidence can't be read. `tmux new-session -d -P -F '#{pid}'` gives the server pid in the same launch.
- tmux leaves the socket pathname after kill-server (3.4 and 3.6a). A fixture Drop must remove the socket and lock, and only once the pid is gone; removing a live server's socket orphans it (`kill-server -L` can't reach it). Mutation runs that break this leak real servers: after them, `ps | grep 'tmux -L pij-'` and kill your own.
- An unlinkable flock file needs the TAKER to re-check after flock that fstat(fd) dev/ino == lstat(path) (else reopen, bounded). Holding the flock across the unlink is not enough.
- Shared-target build stamps: write "running <tree>" before the first cargo command and "finished <tree>" after the last. A batch can build and then fail. Scan every deps dir (--target puts deps at depth 4). Version the stamp format so an old, possibly poisoned stamp never matches. Write through mktemp + mv, never through a link or into a directory.
- Reviewers reproduce with real cargo/tmux. Keep raw logs per run (not just summary lines); performance asks for the raw receipts.
- Tests that `eprintln!` in Drop are silent when they pass, so check for leaks via find -newer on a marker file after the run.
